items.title: What energy-sector expertise can bring to Europe’s emerging carbon removal industry
items.summary: Stockholm Exergi publishes an interview with Carlo Sem, Project Director at Saipem, on the construction of Beccs Stockholm. It covers how energy-sector expertise is being applied to turning carbon removal ambitions into a built bio-CCS plant.
items.why_it_matters: Beccs Stockholm is a key Swedish capture node whose construction progress sets the timing of future CO2 shipping volumes from Stockholm to North Sea storage.

items.title: Polluter pays or taxpayer pays? Weaker EU carbon prices widen the carbon capture funding gap
items.source: Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis (IEEFA)
items.summary: An IEEFA report by Andrew Reid argues that proposed EU ETS changes and lower carbon price forecasts (ABN AMRO's 2030 EUA forecast falling from €145 to €91/tCO2) leave a growing gap against estimated full-chain CCS costs (capture, transport and storage) of €191–265/tCO2. For an illustrative portfolio matching the EU's 50 Mt/yr 2030 injection target, it estimates costs of €351 billion over 25 years and a funding gap that widens from €103 billion to €142 billion, shifting more of the burden to public support.
items.why_it_matters: Gives full-chain CCS cost ranges and ETS-price scenarios that set the revenue side of any Nordic network or contract model, and signals that cross-border chains will lean more on state support schemes than on the carbon price.
